reason: Conversation 1 reasons through the evidence correctly: it asks about fan noise, ties the roaring fan and the newly fitted drawer to restricted ventilation and thermal cut-out, respects the refusal to look underneath, and gives a sensible interim step (stop using high power), while keeping the fan-fault possibility as a conditional rather than a firm claim. Its weakness is the final turn, which never explicitly tells the homeowner to get the fitter/installer or an engineer back to check clearances now that they won't do it themselves. Conversation 2 does escalate to an engineer and avoids any unsupported part claims, but its second reply is dismissive ('Nothing changes'), ignores the key new fact that the fault began exactly when the drawer went in, never asks about the fan or the flashing code, and offers no interim advice, so it serves the homeowner less well despite the cleaner escalation.
